source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: In the bustling hospital corridor, a nurse rushed past the waiting chairs, her heels clicking on the tiled floor. She held the emergency patient’s chart tightly, scanning it as she approached the registration desk. Beside her, a concerned companion sat stiffly, her hand resting on the patient’s arm. Behind them, doctors and nurses moved swiftly through the halls, their strides quick to reach patients needing urgent care. Monitors beeped in rhythm, drip tubes hung from hooks, and curtains were pulled closed over beds. At the desk, a register of clinical urgency buzzed with intercom sounds and the clatter of forms filled the air. A patient’s distressed groans echoed through the corridors, mingling with the occasional wheezing from others awaiting their turn.
